mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best defines "stunted growth" in plants caused by mineral deficiency?

options.A: Reduced overall plant size with short internodes while other parts appear normal.
options.B: Yellowing of older leaves while veins remain green.
options.C: Development of necrotic spots on leaf margins.

mcqs.answer: Reduced overall plant size with short internodes while other parts appear normal.
mcqs.explanation: Stunted growth refers to a marked reduction in the size of the whole plant, especially short internodes, without obvious discoloration or necrosis. Options B, C, and D describe chlorosis, necrosis, and delayed flowering respectively, which are different deficiency symptoms.

mcqs.question: A farmer notices that his wheat crop is flowering much later than usual, although the leaves look healthy. Which mineral deficiency is most likely responsible for this delayed flowering?
mcqs.explanation: Phosphorus deficiency commonly causes delayed maturity and delayed flowering while the foliage may remain relatively normal. Nitrogen deficiency leads to chlorosis, potassium to marginal necrosis, and calcium to tip burn, none of which primarily delay flowering.

mcqs.question: A plant shows interveinal chlorosis in its young leaves while the older leaves remain green. Which mineral deficiency is most directly associated with this symptom?
mcqs.explanation: Iron deficiency characteristically produces interveinal chlorosis in the young, expanding leaves because iron is immobile in the plant. Nitrogen deficiency causes overall yellowing of older leaves, potassium deficiency gives marginal necrosis, and magnesium deficiency leads to interveinal chlorosis in older leaves.

mcqs.question: A farmer observes that the older leaves of his wheat crop turn yellow while the veins stay green, and the younger leaves look normal. Which mineral deficiency is most likely causing this chlorosis?
mcqs.explanation: Nitrogen deficiency typically produces chlorosis (yellowing) of the older leaves first because nitrogen is mobile and moves to younger growth. Iron deficiency affects young leaves, while phosphorus and calcium deficiencies give different symptom patterns.

mcqs.question: True or False: Necrotic lesions on leaf tips are always caused by fungal infection and never by mineral deficiency.

options.C: Both can occur, but fungal infection is more common
options.D: Both are equally likely in all crops

mcqs.explanation: Necrosis can result from deficiencies of potassium or calcium, which cause tip burn and necrotic patches. While fungal infections also cause necrosis, it is incorrect to state that mineral deficiency never leads to necrotic lesions.

mcqs.question: If a plant exhibits pronounced stunted growth but its leaf colour remains normal, which mineral deficiency is the most plausible explanation?
mcqs.explanation: Phosphorus deficiency often leads to severe stunting with dark‑green or normal‑coloured leaves, whereas nitrogen deficiency would also cause chlorosis, iron deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis, and magnesium deficiency gives interveinal chlorosis in older leaves.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a mineral deficiency with its primary symptom of delayed flowering?
mcqs.explanation: Among the listed minerals, phosphorus deficiency is well known to cause delayed maturity and delayed flowering. Boron deficiency mainly affects pollen germination and fruit set, potassium deficiency leads to marginal necrosis, and magnesium deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis, none of which primarily delay flowering.

mcqs.question: A horticulturist notes the following symptoms in a tomato plant: (i) interveinal chlorosis in young leaves, (ii) necrotic spots on leaf margins, and (iii) poor fruit set. Which combination of mineral deficiencies best explains all three observations?

options.A: Iron deficiency, Calcium deficiency, and Phosphorus deficiency
options.B: Nitrogen deficiency, Potassium deficiency, and Boron deficiency
options.C: Magnesium deficiency, Iron deficiency, and Calcium deficiency
options.D: Iron deficiency, Potassium deficiency, and Boron deficiency

mcqs.answer: Iron deficiency, Potassium deficiency, and Boron deficiency
mcqs.explanation: Interveinal chlorosis in young leaves points to iron deficiency. Necrotic spots on leaf margins are typical of potassium deficiency. Poor fruit set is a hallmark of boron deficiency. The combination in option D therefore accounts for all three symptoms, whereas the other options mix unrelated deficiencies.
